2609.16793.title: Available but Unclaimed: An Empirical Study of Human-AI Synergy
2609.16793.paper_summary: People increasingly reason with large language models (LLMs), yet complementary capabilities do not guarantee outperforming both components. In a between-subjects study, participants (N=535) solved a 40-item battery of matrix reasoning, mental rotation, syllogisms, and letter-string analogies, unaided or with GPT-5.6-Luna, Claude Opus 4.8, Gemini 3.6 Flash, or Kimi K3. Each assisted trial required consultation with the model. Each model answered every item alone 100 times under matched elicitation. The assisted-unaided accuracy difference increased with item-level LLM competence. Deference varied across tasks and increased with competence within tasks. Post-advice confidence distinguished correct from incorrect answers less strongly than unaided confidence. In a reference comparison, about half the increase in LLM accuracy carried through to assisted accuracy. How much of that accuracy gain reached participants differed across the models. These findings motivate evaluating LLMs in interaction with humans and designing support for selective deference that preserves independent reasoning.
2609.16793.paper_summary_zh: 人們越來越多地使用大型語言模型（LLMs）進行推理，但互補能力並不保證超越兩個組件。在一項被試間研究中，參與者（N=535）解決了一組40道題目的矩陣推理、心智旋轉、三段論和字母串類比，無輔助或使用GPT-5.6-Luna、Claude Opus 4.8、Gemini 3.6 Flash或Kimi K3。每次輔助試驗都需要與模型進行諮詢。每個模型在匹配引出下獨立回答每個項目100次。輔助與無輔助的準確性差異隨著項目層級的LLM能力增強而增加。對於任務的尊重程度因任務而異，並隨著任務內的能力增強而增加。後續建議的信心對正確與錯誤答案的區分不如無輔助信心強。在參考比較中，大約一半的LLM準確性增長轉化為輔助準確性。這種準確性增益在不同模型之間對參與者的影響有所不同。這些發現激勵我們評估LLMs與人類的互動，並設計支持選擇性尊重的方式，以保持獨立推理。
